what: REVISED committed recommendation for aide-memory binary migration: Bun compile + Option A shim (src/memory/db.ts switching better-sqlite3/bun:sqlite by runtime). Reason for revision from prior "yao-pkg first → Bun later" hybrid: yao-pkg has a material, recurring antivirus false-positive problem because it ships a PATCHED Node binary that ML/heuristic AV engines flag. Maintainer's own words (yao-pkg#156): "the problem is that we are patching nodejs binaries, so our binary is different from the official one and the antivirus may notice this". Issue #167 reporter confirms even signing does not fully resolve. Multi-engine VirusTotal flags persist on Node-22 builds. Bun has ~1/10th the AV headache — runtime is signed by Oven, distinct JSC-based image with SmartScreen reputation. Flagship users confirmed for both (yao-pkg: AWS Amplify / Firebase / Kong / DataDog / Balena; Bun: Claude Code) but the AV delta is qualitative not quantitative. Required infrastructure regardless of compiler choice: Apple Developer Program ($99/yr) + notarytool automation, Azure Artifact Signing for Windows (~$120/yr), SHA256 checksums per release, Microsoft WDSI false-positive submission process, documented manual install path for corporate-proxy-blocked users (npm postinstall downloads fail behind proxies — larksuite/cli#201, cypress-io/cypress#733). Hybrid path (yao-pkg first) rejected because users would eat AV friction during yao-pkg phase — damaging for "private by default" product positioning. Memory 154's architectural invariant (compiler-agnostic CLI) still applies — Bun → yao-pkg migration remains cheap if ever needed. Oscillation note: this recommendation changed 5+ times during session; memory 149 caveat strongly applies to future reviewers — verify AV claims and decision rationale before accepting final call.
why: AV research this turn revealed a qualitative delta I hadn't investigated — yao-pkg's patched-Node triggers recurring AV flags that Bun mostly avoids. Updating the committed recommendation since this factor is material for user experience on a "private by default" product. Also documenting the oscillation explicitly so future spawns see the churn pattern and apply extra scrutiny.
